approach: Add run/format.rs with `format_work_tree(dir, changes: &[DiffEntry], ctx: &CheckContext)`, Athena host code and not an agent command. When `dir/Cargo.toml` is a file and the change list holds a non-deleted `*.rs` entry, it runs `cargo fmt --all` and then `cargo fmt --all --check`, both through `checks::run_check`. It returns `Skipped(reason)`, `Done`, `Unfixed{output, note}` or `Stopped(note)`. `Stopped` is returned when the kill switch is set or a run hit its deadline. `producer_loop` calls it in every pass, right after the producer's report is parsed and before the first `snapshot.change_list()` (producer.rs:339). In this plan "after the producer" means after each producer pass and before the change list is taken (round-1 finding 1). The unmet, unchanged-file, scope, decision-gate and mirror checks, `loop_replay` and the later candidate, checks and verifier then all see the same formatted tree. format.rs's module docs say this, so whoever checks criterion 3 judges it against the reading's "end of producer_loop, before the change list". Answers to the round-2 findings. (1) Every test that runs real cargo fmt under the cleared env also writes the repository's pinned `rust-toolchain.toml` into the tree, so rustup resolves 1.97.0 with rustfmt as it does for Athena's own checks. This covers the unit-test temp crates and the end-to-end base, where the file is committed with `commit_file`. (2) A set kill switch or a deadline hit returns `Stopped`, and `producer_loop` closes the job through `self.failure` and returns `Flow::Stop`, like its other stop points. (3) The step keeps `cargo fmt --all`. A pure helper `paths_added_by_format(before, after)` finds paths the formatter added beyond the pre-step change list, and a UI line names them. (4) The registry is bound before the `CheckContext` is built, as mod.rs:1949 does. Root cause: the producer's grant allows `cargo fmt` (policy.rs:680 denies it only to roles that cannot write), but only prose asks the producer to run it and nothing makes the tree formatted before the gate.

decisions.choice: Run the format step in each producer pass, after the report is parsed (after the `raw` match, producer.rs:325-335) and before `let changes = snapshot.change_list()?` (producer.rs:339). Take a first change list for the guard, format, and let line 339 read the list again.
decisions.reason: `loop_replay` (producer.rs:370) stores the tree it measured, and `replay_run` reuses it only if `covers` holds. Formatting after the loop would change the candidate tree and force a rebuild of the replay pair. It would also leave the scope, gate and mirror send-back checks judging a tree that is not the candidate. Before line 339 every in-loop reader sees the candidate tree, and the step is still after the producer and before the checks and verifier (criterion 3). It is idempotent, so a send-back pass formats again cheaply.

rejected.option: Format once after the loop, before `Ok(Flow::Go(..))`
rejected.why: The replay tree no longer matches the candidate, and the in-loop checks judge an unformatted tree. A path the formatter adds ends the job at check_and_verify with no send-back.
Same stale-tree problem, and it splits the producer stage across two files.

rejected.option: Also format after the TimedOut or non-Success early returns
rejected.why: Those paths stop the job and keep or discard the work as it is. A tree-seeded retry is formatted when its own producer pass finishes.

decisions.choice: Run both cargo invocations through `crate::checks::run_check` with `CheckSpec{name:"format", kind: CheckKind::Command, skip_when_only: None}`. The env is `athena_agent::env::build` with `Side::Produce` and the timeout is `budget.check_timeout_s`. In producer_loop, `let registry = self.state.registry();` is bound before the `CheckContext` literal.
decisions.reason: It reuses tested code for timeout, process-group kill, kill switch, registry and the output tail, so an Unfixed output has the shape of a failed fmt check record, which criterion 2 compares. Binding the registry first fixes the temporary-borrow compile error (finding 4), as mod.rs:1949 does.

rejected.why: `run_bounded` drops output, so the error text of criterion 2 would be lost, and it has no kill switch or redaction.

rejected.option: Use the producer spec.env with CargoShim
rejected.why: The shim takes a build slot for build, test, clippy and check. fmt builds nothing, so a slot wait would hold the job for no reason.
It borrows a temporary that is used after the statement and does not compile.

decisions.choice: Take `&[athena_git::DiffEntry]`. Skip unless `dir/Cargo.toml` is a file and some entry has `status != 'D'` and a path ending in `.rs`. Tests build entries with a helper `entry(status, path)`.
decisions.reason: One signature that production and tests share, and the status is available for the deleted-file case. The `.rs` guard keeps a docs-only or Cargo.toml-only job from rewriting base files outside its scope.

rejected.why: Needs conversion in production, or loses the status that the deleted-file test needs.
A job with no Rust change could grow its diff by base layout drift and fail the scope check.

decisions.choice: Handle a stop. Before running anything, and again after each run, `format_work_tree` returns `Formatted::Stopped(note)` if `ctx.registry.stopped()` is true or `checks::timed_out(&run)` is true. `producer_loop` then does `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &format!("the format step stopped: {note}")); return Ok(Flow::Stop);`, the same shape as producer.rs:292-294 and 332-333.
decisions.reason: Finding 2. run_check reports a kill-switch kill as a failed run with a note and exit_code None (checks.rs:577-583, 591), not as an error. Without this the stopped job would go on into loop_replay, the checks and the candidate as if the formatter had merely failed. A check that hit its deadline is a hung tool, not an unfixable layout error, so it also stops the job with the reason.

rejected.option: Map every failed `--check` run to Unfixed
rejected.why: It hides a stop from the loop, which keeps running a job the user has stopped.

rejected.option: Return an Err from format_work_tree on stop
rejected.why: An Err from producer_loop does not carry a closing reason; `self.failure` records the reason the way the other stop points do.

decisions.choice: An Unfixed result changes no flow. It prints one UI line `format     cargo fmt --check still fails: <first output line>; the fmt check will report it` and leaves the tree. When `work_tree_tree()` differs after the step, it prints `format     cargo fmt rewrote the work tree before the checks`. It also calls `snapshot.change_list()` and prints `format     cargo fmt also changed <paths> beyond the producer's files` for any path from the pure helper `paths_added_by_format(before, after)`.
decisions.reason: The reading says unfixable errors stay in the tree and the normal fmt check reports them; a second reporting path could relax the gate. Naming added paths answers finding 3 at its stated minimum, and the in-loop scope check, which runs after the step, still sends the producer back for a path outside its allowed paths.

rejected.option: Narrow the rewrite to the job's files with `rustfmt --edition <ed> <files>` or `cargo fmt -- <files>`
rejected.why: rustfmt run on a file also formats its out-of-line `mod` children. Plain rustfmt does not read the package edition, so the edition would have to be guessed, and the result could differ from what `cargo fmt --all --check` accepts. The check could then still fail. The guard plus the added-paths line and the scope check cover the case.

rejected.option: Send the producer back with the rustfmt error
rejected.why: It adds a send-back class beyond one focused step. Left as a User: question.

rejected.option: Fail the job at the step
rejected.why: It would duplicate the fmt check and bypass the baseline pre-existing comparison (`mark_pre_existing`).

decisions.choice: Leave crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs and all config untouched. Describe the root cause as in the approach.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 and Out of scope. The producer already has the `cargo fmt` grant (athena.toml:74 lists fmt in producer_commands), and the verifier's deny binds only roles that cannot write. The step is host code spawning a process, not a Bash command through the hook.

rejected.option: Change the policy to allow fmt for more roles
rejected.why: Out of scope, and the producer already has the grant.

rejected.option: Add a prompt rule telling the producer to run cargo fmt
rejected.why: Prose is the failing mechanism; the user default says enforce by mechanism.

decisions.choice: Every test that runs real cargo fmt writes the pinned toolchain file. A helper `temp_crate(files)` writes Cargo.toml, src files and `include_str!("../../../../rust-toolchain.toml")` as rust-toolchain.toml. The end-to-end test calls `commit_file(&repo, "rust-toolchain.toml", include_str!(...))`, Cargo.toml and a clean src/lib.rs on the base. The unit `CheckContext` env takes PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN from the process when set.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. run_check clears the env (checks.rs:534), the end-to-end env passes only HOME and PATH plus RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME when set (athena.toml:52-58), and nothing sets RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN. Without a toolchain file, a host whose rustup has no default toolchain (setup.sh installs with `--default-toolchain none`) would fail to start cargo fmt, and a host with another default would use a different rustfmt. With the file (channel 1.97.0, components clippy and rustfmt) rustup resolves the pinned toolchain from the directory, as for Athena's own checks.

rejected.option: Pass RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN only in the unit tests' CheckContext
rejected.why: It does not cover the end-to-end job, whose env comes from athena.toml.

rejected.option: Inherit the full process env in tests
rejected.why: It would not exercise the cleared env that real checks and the step use.

decisions.reason: The deliverable list names tests.rs, and the end-to-end helpers are private to it.

rejected.why: The fake-driver helpers are private to tests.rs.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/run/format.rs. Define `pub(super) enum Formatted { Skipped(&'static str), Done, Unfixed { output: String, note: Option<String> }, Stopped(String) }` and `pub(super) fn format_work_tree(dir: &Path, changes: &[athena_git::DiffEntry], ctx: &CheckContext<'_>) -> Result<Formatted>`. Return Skipped when `dir/Cargo.toml` is not a file or when no entry has `status != 'D'` and a path ending in `.rs`. Return Stopped when `ctx.registry.stopped()` before running. Otherwise `run_check` a `CheckSpec{name:"format", run:["cargo","fmt","--all"], kind: CheckKind::Command, skip_when_only: None}` and ignore its pass or fail. If `ctx.registry.stopped()` or `checks::timed_out(&run)`, return Stopped with the run's note. Then `run_check` the `--check` form with the same stop handling. Return Done if it passed, else Unfixed with the check's `output_tail` and `note`. Also add `pub(super) fn paths_added_by_format(before: &[DiffEntry], after: &[DiffEntry]) -> Vec<String>` returning sorted paths in `after` that are not in `before`. The module docs give the root cause and the meaning of "after the producer".
In crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs add `mod format;` among the module declarations (about lines 61-68).

In producer.rs, inside the loop after the `raw` match (line 335) and before `let unmet` (336), add the step. Skip when `ctx.pin_dir.is_some()`. Otherwise build `env` with `athena_agent::env::build(&EnvSpec{agents:&jc.config.agents, job:id.as_str(), job_dir:&job_dir, snapshot:snapshot.dir(), side:Side::Produce, capability_env:&capability_env}, |k| std::env::var(k).ok()).map_err(anyhow::Error::msg)?`. Bind `let registry = self.state.registry();` first, then build the `CheckContext{dir: snapshot.dir(), env:&env, timeout: Duration::from_secs(jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s), registry:&registry, job:id.as_str(), redactor: ctx.redactor}`. Take `before = snapshot.work_tree_tree()?` and `pre = snapshot.change_list()?`, then `match format::format_work_tree(snapshot.dir(), &pre, &fctx)?`. On Stopped, set `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, &format!("the format step stopped: {note}"))` and `return Ok(Flow::Stop)`. On Unfixed, print the `format` line with the first output line. When `work_tree_tree()` differs afterwards, print the rewrote line, read `snapshot.change_list()` and print the added-paths line if `paths_added_by_format(&pre, &after)` is not empty. Leave the existing `let changes = snapshot.change_list()?` at line 339 to read the list again. Extend the `producer_loop` doc comment.

Write the CHANGELOG.md bullet under `## [Unreleased]`: a job whose only defect is rustfmt layout reaches the verifier formatted. The root cause is that the producer may run `cargo fmt` but nothing made the tree formatted before the gate. Athena now runs `cargo fmt` then `cargo fmt --check` on the work tree after each producer pass, only when a `.rs` file changed. An unfixable error still fails the fmt check, a stopped job stops, and agent policy is unchanged.

In run/tests.rs add to `produce_and_verify_order_tests`: a `FMT_CHECK` const (`["cargo","fmt","--all","--check"]`), an `entry(status: char, path: &str) -> DiffEntry` helper, a `temp_crate` helper that writes Cargo.toml, src files and `include_str!("../../../../rust-toolchain.toml")` as rust-toolchain.toml, and a unit `CheckContext` helper whose env takes PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN from the process when set. Add the unit tests for criteria 1, 2 and 5, the stop test and the added-paths test. Add the end-to-end test for criteria 3 and 4: `commit_file` Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml and a clean src/lib.rs, a script wrapper setting the producer turn's edits for README.md and a mis-formatted src/lib.rs, `athena_with(.., FMT_CHECK, ..)`, `go`, then assert Landed, the candidate changes, `show_file` equality and a `format` UI line.

Also run `cargo test -p athena-core`, `cargo test -p athena-agent` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle --test retry --test drain --test mirrors`. Confirm `git status` shows only the five deliverables.

No refusal or matching rule is added or changed, so no refusal_corpus case is mapped. `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is run only as a regression guard; this plan cites no corpus case ids because it read none. No step calls an external service.

risks.risk: The tests run real cargo fmt under a cleared env. On a host with no rustup default toolchain, or a different default, cargo fmt could fail to start or use another rustfmt (round-2 finding 1).
risks.mitigation: Every temp crate and the end-to-end base carry the repository's pinned rust-toolchain.toml (1.97.0 with rustfmt), so rustup resolves the pinned toolchain from the directory as for Athena's own checks. The unit env also passes RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN when set. A host without that toolchain fails the tests rather than skipping, as it already fails its own fmt check.

risks.risk: The base is not fmt-clean, so `cargo fmt --all` rewrites files the producer never touched and adds paths outside the job's allowed paths (finding 3).
risks.mitigation: The step runs only when a non-deleted `.rs` entry is already in the change list. A UI line names any path it adds, and the in-loop scope check, which runs after the step, can send the producer back. The reading accepts the clean-base assumption, and the changelog bullet notes it.

risks.risk: A kill switch or hung fmt could be mistaken for a layout error and the job would go on.
risks.mitigation: The Stopped outcome ends the job through `self.failure` and `Flow::Stop`, and the stop test covers it.

risks.risk: `cargo fmt` may write a Cargo.lock in the end-to-end tree, which would show in the change list and break the exact-changes assertion.
risks.mitigation: `cargo fmt` reads `cargo metadata --no-deps`, which resolves nothing, and the test dependency-free crate has nothing to lock. If a lock file still appears when the producer first runs the test, the base commits one with `commit_file`. The assertion names the full list so any such path is seen.

risks.risk: Formatting every pass costs two cargo runs per producer invocation.
risks.mitigation: The cost is a few seconds with no build, the step is idempotent, and a producer rarely has more than two passes (`PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`).

risks.risk: A pinned study mounts a checkout inside the work tree (producer.rs:147-149), and formatting would alter pinned files.
rustfmt output varies by toolchain version, so literal expected text could drift.
risks.mitigation: The pinned toolchain file fixes the version in tests. Test 1 uses stable constructs (a long array and `fn f( )->u32{1}`) and proves success with the post `--check` pass, plus a literal only for the simple function body.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `a_misformatted_rust_file_is_rewritten_and_cargo_fmt_check_then_passes` in run/tests.rs. A `temp_crate` helper writes Cargo.toml, rust-toolchain.toml (the repository's pinned file) and a src/lib.rs with a long `pub const` array on one line and `fn f( )->u32{1}`. The CheckContext takes its env from the process (PATH, HOME, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN when set), with `Registry::new(tempdir)` and `Redactor::new(&athena_gate::builtin_config())`. The test runs `run_check` with `cargo fmt --all --check` and asserts it fails. It then calls `format_work_tree(dir, &[entry('M',"src/lib.rs")], &ctx)` and asserts `Done`, that the file text changed to rustfmt layout, and that `cargo fmt --all --check` through `run_check` now passes.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core a_misformatted_rust_file_is_rewritten_and_cargo_fmt_check_then_passes && cargo test -p athena-core
demonstrations.observes: The file bytes change to the formatted layout, the outcome is Done, and the fmt check goes from failed to passed. The whole athena-core suite passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the formatter run the file stays mis-formatted, so the content assertion, the Done assertion and the post-`--check` assertion all fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `run::format::format_work_tree` (added by plan step 1), called with a real `CheckContext` over a tempdir and real `cargo fmt` resolved by the written rust-toolchain.toml. Guards: Cargo.toml present and a non-deleted `.rs` entry. No double. `checks::run_check` exists (checks.rs:513). The test and the `temp_crate` and `entry` helpers are added by step 6.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `an_unfixable_fmt_error_is_reported_and_the_fmt_check_fails_with_the_same_text`. The temp crate's src/lib.rs is `pub fn broken( {` (a parse error). `format_work_tree` with `entry('M',"src/lib.rs")` must return `Unfixed{output, ..}` whose `output` holds a line starting `error` and the name `lib.rs`. `run_check` with the configured fmt spec `cargo fmt --all --check` on the same dir must give `!passed`, and its `output_tail` must contain the step's first `error` line. The broken file must be byte-identical afterwards.
demonstrations.observes: A failed fmt result whose rustfmt error text appears in the failed check's output tail. The tree is not changed and the gate is not relaxed.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the step swallowed the failure and returned Done, the Unfixed assertion fails. If it rewrote or deleted the broken file, the byte-identity assertion fails. If the check's output tail did not carry the error text, the contains assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `format_work_tree` (step 1) plus `checks::run_check` (exists), with real cargo and rustfmt in a tempdir containing the pinned toolchain file. No double. Test added by step 6.

demonstrations.method: Two parts. (a) Content: Grep crates/athena-core/src/run for `format_work_tree` and `change_list`. The format.rs module docs state that "after the producer" means after each producer pass and before the change list (round-1 finding 1). demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `Athena::go` on the fake driver, as in `produce_and_verify_order_tests`. `athena_with(repo, state, checks, plenty_of_space, script)` (tests.rs:187), `base_script()` (tests.rs:219) and `commit_file` (tests.rs:341) exist. Step 6 adds a `FMT_CHECK` const (`cargo fmt --all --check`) and a script wrapper in the style of `each_job_its_own_edit` (tests.rs:4071) whose producer turn sets `edits` for README.md and a mis-formatted src/lib.rs. Real cargo fmt runs in both the step and the check. The stop test uses `Registry::new` and `Registry::stop_file()` (procs.rs:357-365), which exist, and creates the STOP file directly.

demonstrations.method: The same end-to-end test, after `go`: load `Records::load(&athena.git, &athena.head())`, take `jobs[id].candidate`, and assert `candidate.changes` lists README.md and src/lib.rs and nothing else. If `cargo fmt` writes a Cargo.lock, the base commits one. Assert `athena.git.show_file(candidate_commit, "src/lib.rs")` equals the formatted text, not the text the fake producer wrote. Assert the `Lines` capture holds a line starting `format`. A pure test, `paths_added_by_format_names_only_new_paths`, checks the added-paths helper.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core a_job_whose_only_defect_is_rustfmt_layout_passes_a_cargo_fmt_check_and_the_candidate_holds_the_formatted_file && cargo test -p athena-core paths_added_by_format_names_only_new_paths
demonstrations.observes: The recorded candidate commit holds the formatter's bytes, so the change list and diff are of the formatted tree.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the formatter ran on a copy, or after the change list was taken, `show_file` returns the producer's mis-formatted text and the equality assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `Athena::go` with the fake driver, as in criterion 3. `build_candidate` (candidate.rs:34) reads `snapshot.change_list()` after the loop (exists). The test reads the stored candidate record and `Git::show_file` (used near tests.rs 4718-4726; exists). The additions are the script edits and the pure helper (steps 1 and 6).

demonstrations.method: Unit test `a_work_tree_without_cargo_toml_or_a_changed_rust_file_is_not_formatted` writes a mis-formatted src/lib.rs with no Cargo.toml and calls `format_work_tree` with `entry('M',"src/lib.rs")`. It then adds Cargo.toml and calls it with only `entry('M',"README.md")`, and with only `entry('D',"src/lib.rs")`. All three must return `Skipped(..)` and leave the file byte-identical. Content part: `git diff --stat` shows no change to crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs, and format.rs spawns only through `run_check` from host code with no agent grant. The policy tests for `cargo fmt` (policy.rs near 1231-1235) stay green.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core a_work_tree_without_cargo_toml_or_a_changed_rust_file_is_not_formatted && cargo test -p athena-agent
demonstrations.observes: Three Skipped outcomes with unchanged bytes, and an unchanged policy file with its tests green.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the Cargo.toml or the non-deleted-`.rs` guard were missing, the mis-formatted file would be rewritten and the byte-identity assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: `format_work_tree` (step 1), real tempdir, no double. Test added by step 6. The policy tests exist.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG diff. Under `## [Unreleased]` one bullet states that a job whose only defect is rustfmt layout now reaches the verifier formatted, because Athena runs `cargo fmt` and then `cargo fmt --check` on the producer's work tree after each producer pass. It names the root cause (the producer may run `cargo fmt`, but only prose asked it to and nothing formatted the tree before the gate) and says an unfixable fmt error still fails the fmt check.
demonstrations.observes: The new bullet sits in the Unreleased section and the diff touches only that section.

demonstrations.method: Run the three workspace commands in this order after `cargo fmt --all` has formatted the new code and tests.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. The new tests pass. Existing fake-job tests, whose repo has no Cargo.toml, return Skipped and print nothing. The slot test at tests.rs:4185 edits README.md only (each_job_its_own_edit), so it is Skipped too.
demonstrations.fails_without: A failing new test, a clippy warning or an unformatted new file makes the matching command exit non-zero.
demonstrations.seam: The workspace's own checks; no double. Real cargo fmt in the new tests resolves the pinned toolchain from the written rust-toolchain.toml (finding 1).
